messages.author: 4f32321b84c72be4
messages.subject: ggplot2 facets error
parts:
Following  is the small part of my dataset. which has four columns: "POPULATION2013","EDUCATION","County","State".I want to plot population versus education using ggplot2 with facets as the State and its respective counties. Here in the dataset the states are USA states.In that way I should get 50 subplots with the facets.


  POPULATION2013     EDUCATION         County         State
1          55246               21.7               Autauga County    AL
2         195540              27.7                Baldwin County    AL
3          27076              14.5                 Barbour County    AL
4          22512                 9.0                   Bibb County    AL
5          57872                 12.4               Blount County    AL
6          10639                 11.9              Bullock County    AL

But when I use the following command.

sp <- ggplot(t, aes(x=EDUCATION, y=POPULATION2013)) + geom_point(shape=1)
sp + facet_grid(. ~ State)


I am getting the following error

Error in layout_base(data, cols, drop = drop) : 
  At least one layer must contain all variables used for facetting

Where am I going wrong, how can I get the plot with facets as the different states?

parts:
Here's my code and the data sets (DataSet.txt and FIPS_CountyName.txt) from which I collected 2013 population estimate and people who have completed Bachelors degree.

censusdata <- read.table("DataSet.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
censusfips <- read.fwf("FIPS_CountyName.txt", c(5, -1, 100))
census <- merge(censusdata, censusfips, by.x="fips", by.y=1)
keeps <- c("PST045213","EDU685212","V2")
table=census[keeps]
colnames(table) <- c("POPULATION2013", "EDUCATION","V2")
t=table[grepl(",",table$V2),]
t$County <- lapply(strsplit(as.character(t$V2), "\\,"), "[", 1)
t$State<- lapply(strsplit(as.character(t$V2), "\\,"), "[", 2)
t$V2<-NULL
rownames(t) <- 1:nrow(t)
library(ggplot2)
sp <- ggplot(t, aes(x=EDUCATION, y=POPULATION2013)) + geom_point(shape=1) + facet_grid(. ~ State)

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 facets error
parts:
The answer is in the data frame `t`, not the ggplot code: look at it
using str(t) or summary(t)! You'll see that the "Country" and "State"
columns are actually lists within the data frame, because you're
assigning the results of lapply to those columns--but lapply returns a
list, not a vector. So change these two lines:

t$County <- unlist(lapply(strsplit(as.character(t$V2), "\\,"), "[", 1))
t$State<- unlist(lapply(strsplit(as.character(t$V2), "\\,"), "[", 2))

...and things will work better.

Ben

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 facets error
parts:
I changed your data frame name t to tt because t() is the commonly
used transpose function, and it's just safe to avoid name duplication.
The other problem was that strsplit() returns a list. Convert those to
character instead:

tt=table[grepl(",",table$V2),]
tt$County <- as.character(lapply(strsplit(as.character(tt$V2), "\\,"), "[", 1))
tt$State<- as.character(lapply(strsplit(as.character(tt$V2), "\\,"), "[", 2))
tt$V2<-NULL
rownames(tt) <- 1:nrow(tt)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(tt, aes(x=EDUCATION, y=POPULATION2013)) +
geom_point(shape=1) +
facet_wrap( ~ State)

You don't want to use facet_grid() with one dimension and 50+ levels.
It's probably useful to remove DC from the data set since it contains
only one observation.

Dennis

On Tue, Dec 8, 2015 at 3:10 AM, Ben Bond-Lamberty <bpb...@gmail.com> wrote:
The answer is in the data frame `t`, not the ggplot code: look at it
using str(t) or summary(t)! You'll see that the "Country" and "State"
columns are actually lists within the data frame, because you're
assigning the results of lapply to those columns--but lapply returns a
list, not a vector. So change these two lines:

t$County <- unlist(lapply(strsplit(as.character(t$V2), "\\,"), "[", 1))
t$State<- unlist(lapply(strsplit(as.character(t$V2), "\\,"), "[", 2))

...and things will work better.

Ben

parts:
Thanks Dennis,

It works.Now I got it, where exactly I went wrong.

On Tue, Dec 8, 2015 at 3:16 AM, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
I changed your data frame name t to tt because t() is the commonly
used transpose function, and it's just safe to avoid name duplication.
The other problem was that strsplit() returns a list. Convert those to
character instead:

tt=table[grepl(",",table$V2),]
tt$County <- as.character(lapply(strsplit(as.character(tt$V2), "\\,"), "[", 1))
tt$State<- as.character(lapply(strsplit(as.character(tt$V2), "\\,"), "[", 2))
tt$V2<-NULL
rownames(tt) <- 1:nrow(tt)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(tt, aes(x=EDUCATION, y=POPULATION2013)) +
        geom_point(shape=1) +
        facet_wrap( ~ State)

You don't want to use facet_grid() with one dimension and 50+ levels.
It's probably useful to remove DC from the data set since it contains
only one observation.

Dennis
